paragraphs: A coastal province recently required restaurants to print the calorie content of every dish on their menus. Researchers then compared the receipts of a large restaurant chain's outlets in the province with those of the same chain's outlets in a neighboring province that had no such rule. In the year after the requirement took effect, the average calorie content of the meals ordered fell by 6 percent in the first province and was essentially unchanged in the second. The researchers conclude that calorie labeling leads diners to choose lighter meals, and they recommend that the neighboring province adopt the same rule.
